The structure of K2ErFeO6 crystallizes in the tetragonal space group I-4m2 (No. 119), with a unit cell containing 20 atoms (K4Er2Fe2O12) and six independent Wyckoff orbits. Geometry-derived analysis identifies Er and Fe each as octahedral centers coordinated by six O neighbors, while K adopts a close-packed-like 12-coordinate arrangement. Corner-sharing is observed between Er and Fe octahedra, and face-sharing occurs between the 12-vertex K polyhedra and both octahedral types. The geometric neighbor graph forms a single three-dimensional component spanning all 20 sites.
